<div align="center">

<p>Nigeria’s largest private refinery, the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, has assured Nigerians that there will be enough fuel in the country despite the ongoing crisis in the Middle East affecting global oil supply.</p><div class='ai-viewports ai-viewport-2 ai-viewport-3 ai-insert-17-71917573' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;' data-insertion-position='prepend' data-selector='.ai-insert-17-71917573' data-insertion-no-dbg data-code='' data-block='17'></div>


<p>In a statement released on Thursday, the company said it will focus on supplying petrol and other refined products to the Nigerian market first.</p>
<p>It explained that this step will help protect the country from global fuel shortages caused by the conflict in the Middle East.</p><div class='code-block code-block-18' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;'>
<div align="center">
<!-- /14001636/DP_InsidePost_Adsense_2 -->
<div id='div-gpt-ad-1524595905268-5'>
<script>
googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-1524595905268-5'); });
</script>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<p>The refinery said the crisis has forced some refineries in other countries to shut down, reducing the amount of fuel available worldwide.</p>
<p>It added that China has also stopped exporting petrol and diesel, which has increased pressure on the global fuel supply.</p><div class='ai-viewports ai-viewport-2 ai-viewport-3 ai-insert-19-13492033' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;' data-insertion-position='prepend' data-selector='.ai-insert-19-13492033' data-insertion-no-dbg data-code='' data-block='19'></div>


<p>According to the company, having a large refinery in Nigeria helps the country avoid the full impact of international disruptions because more fuel can now be refined locally instead of relying on imports.</p>
<p>The refinery noted that global oil prices have increased sharply due to the crisis. It said the price of Brent crude has risen by about 26 per cent to more than $84 per barrel.</p>
<p>Because of these rising costs, the company increased its petrol price at the depot by N100 per litre, which is about a 12 per cent rise. However, it said it absorbed about 20 per cent of the additional cost to reduce the burden on consumers.</p><div class='ai-viewports ai-viewport-2 ai-viewport-3 ai-insert-20-19423748' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;' data-insertion-position='prepend' data-selector='.ai-insert-20-19423748' data-insertion-no-dbg data-code='' data-block='20'></div>


<p>The refinery explained that it buys crude oil at international market prices, whether the supply comes from Nigeria or other countries. Nigerian crude is usually priced between $3 and $6 above the Brent benchmark, while shipping costs add about $3.50 per barrel.</p>
<p>As a result, crude oil now reaches the refinery at between $88 and $91 per barrel. Previously, the cost was around $68 per barrel when petrol was sold at N774 per litre.</p>
<p>The company also said it receives about five cargoes of crude oil every month from the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, which are paid for in naira. However, the refinery needs about 13 cargoes monthly to meet Nigeria’s fuel demand.</p><div class='ai-viewports ai-viewport-2 ai-viewport-3 ai-insert-21-88146494' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;' data-insertion-position='prepend' data-selector='.ai-insert-21-88146494' data-insertion-no-dbg data-code='' data-block='21'></div>


<p>“This is one of the many benefits of domestic refining,” the company stated, adding that large-scale local refining significantly reduces the country’s vulnerability to international supply disruptions,” it added.</p>
<p>Because of the shortfall, it has to buy additional crude oil from international traders using foreign exchange.</p>
<p>Despite these challenges, the refinery said large-scale local refining will help reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imports and protect the country from severe fuel shortages during global crises.</p>
<p>The company also revealed plans to improve fuel distribution across the country by introducing trucks powered by compressed natural gas (CNG).</p>
<p>It said the rollout of the CNG trucks will begin this month to speed up delivery and reduce transport costs.</p><div class='ai-viewports ai-viewport-2 ai-viewport-3 ai-insert-23-60066582' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;' data-insertion-position='prepend' data-selector='.ai-insert-23-60066582' data-insertion-no-dbg data-code='' data-block='23'></div>

New data shows <a ref="dofollow" data-ga-onclick="Inarticle articleshow link click#News#href" href="/topic/diesel-prices" target="_blank">diesel prices</a> are moving close to a two-year peak in the U.S. as tensions in the Middle East affect oil supply and markets. The national average price of diesel reached $4.00 per gallon on Wednesday, the first time it has touched this level since April 24, 2024, according to Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy.<br><br><style>

        		    </style><!--/budget_surveybanner.cms?msid=126369359&type=showpotime:2--><br><h2>Rising fuel prices in the US</h2>Rising fuel prices are also putting pressure on the administration of Donald Trump, as energy costs are often linked to political debates and election outcomes. The recent military strikes on Iran and Iran’s large-scale retaliation strategy have shaken global oil markets and raised fears about supply disruptions. Experts warn that these tensions could push fuel prices higher depending on how long the conflict continues.<div id="E_3" class="etoro" style="height:auto; width:650px; margin: 2px 0 10px;"></div><br><div class="adBox custom_ad nonm taboola" data-taboola="taboola_129104113"><div class="colombia colombiaAd" data-section="0" data-position="129104113" data-slot="532740" col="2" id="div-clmb-ctn-208630-129104113-26" data-msg="ctnCallbackHandler" data1-nextStory="0"></div><div class="et_vdoai" id="v-economictimes-indiatimes-v3"></div><div data-placement="Mid Article Thumbnails" data-target_type="mix" data-mode="thumbnails-mid" style="min-height:400px; margin-bottom:12px;" class="wdt-taboola" id="taboola-mid-article-thumbnails-129104113"></div></div><br>The latest data from AAA shows that diesel prices have now climbed to $4.17 per gallon as of early Thursday morning. This new price is much higher than $3.66 per gallon recorded at the same time last year, according to AAA data cited by Newsweek. However, diesel prices are still lower than the record average of $5.82 per gallon, which happened in summer 2022 after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Analysts say the rise in pump prices usually follows global oil price increases, but it often takes days or weeks before consumers fully feel the change.<br><br><h2>Global oil prices continue to climb</h2>Global oil benchmark Brent crude is currently trading at around $83 per barrel. Analysts warn that oil prices could climb above $100 per barrel, a level not seen since 2022, if shipping disruptions in the Gulf region continue. A key risk point is the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway where about one-fifth of the world’s oil supply passes through. Shipping in this vital route has been disrupted because of the conflict, which has slowed oil transport and worried global markets.<br><style>

Because of repeated drone attacks, several oil refineries have been forced to stop their operations, according to Newsweek. Torbjorn Soltvedt, a Middle East analyst at Verisk Maplecroft, said the situation is very serious because key energy facilities are now being directly targeted. Soltvedt explained that the global oil market is in a risky situation. Energy facilities are being attacked, and shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has almost stopped. He also warned that oil prices could continue to rise if the United States and Israel do not stop Iran from launching more drones and missiles.<br><div data-msid="129104113" class="masterclass_carousel"></div><div data-msid="129104113" class="as_freetrial_widget"></div><br><div data-size="[[300, 250], [600, 250], [600, 300]]" data-adsSlot="/7176/Economictimes/ET_News/ET_News_InternationalBusiness/ET_ROS_MID_NWS_IBZ_AS_300" data-loc="100" id="div-gpt-ad-858478126-129104113" style="text-align: center;" class="country_specAD"></div><h2>US plans steps to stabilize oil supply</h2>Soltvedt explained that oil supply problems have been limited so far because Gulf countries exported large amounts of oil earlier to prepare for possible conflict disruptions. However, he warned that this early export strategy will lose its effect in the coming weeks, which could make supply shortages worse, according to Soltvedt’s statement to Newsweek. He added that if Iranian attacks on Gulf energy sites and threats to shipping continue for two more weeks, oil prices reaching $100 per barrel could become a realistic possibility. <br><br><div data-size="[[300, 250], [600, 250], [600, 300]]" data-adsSlot="/7176/Economictimes/ET_News/ET_News_InternationalBusiness/ET_ROS_MID1_NWS_IBZ_AS_300" data-loc="2" id="div-gpt-ad-858478132-129104113" class="country_specAD2nd"></div><div data-size="[[300, 250], [600, 250], [600, 300]]" data-adsSlot="/7176/Economictimes/ET_News/ET_News_InternationalBusiness/ET_ROS_MID1_NWS_IBZ_AS_300" data-loc="5" id="div-gpt-ad-858478132-129104113" class="country_specAD2nd"></div><div data-size="[[300, 250], [600, 250], [600, 300]]" data-adsSlot="/7176/Economictimes/ET_News/ET_News_InternationalBusiness/ET_ROS_MID1_NWS_IBZ_AS_300" data-loc="3" id="div-gpt-ad-858478132-129104113" class="country_specAD2nd"></div>President Donald Trump said during a Wednesday press conference that the U.S. was performing very well in the war effort. Trump said that if the situation was rated on a scale of 1 to 10, he would rate it “about a 15”. Analysts at Goldman Sachs warned that the ongoing oil price surge could also push inflation higher in the United States later this year. Higher oil prices usually increase transportation and production costs, which then raise prices for many goods and services across the economy.<br><br>On Wednesday, Scott Bessent said the government was preparing a series of announcements about plans to support oil supply flows in the region. These steps are meant to reduce supply risks and stabilize energy markets during the ongoing Middle East conflict, according to Bessent’s statement cited by Newsweek. <br><br>Earlier in the week, Trump also announced that the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation would offer political risk insurance and guarantees for maritime trade in the Gulf. The plan aims to protect ships and companies moving oil through the region during the conflict. Trump also said that if the situation becomes more dangerous, the United States Navy could escort oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz to keep global oil shipments moving safely. <br><br><h2>FAQs</h2><b>Q1. Why are diesel and gas prices rising in the United States?</b><br><br>Fuel prices are rising because the Iran conflict has pushed global oil prices higher and disrupted supply routes like the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysts.<br><br><b>Q2. 			  "mainEntityOfPage":"https://m.economictimes.com/news/international/us/fuel-costs-climb-in-us-diesel-hits-4-a-gallon-amid-iran-war-and-surging-global-oil-prices/articleshow/129104113.cms",
			  
			  "articleSection" : "News",
			  "articleBody":"Fuel prices in the United States are rising again as the ongoing Iran war pushes global oil prices higher. New data shows diesel prices are moving close to a two-year peak in the U.S. as tensions in the Middle East affect oil supply and markets. The national average price of diesel reached $4.00 per gallon on Wednesday, the first time it has touched this level since April 24, 2024, according to Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy.Separate data shows that regular gasoline prices are also rising and moving further above the $3 per gallon mark, according to GasBuddy figures cited by Newsweek. Gasoline futures contracts are also getting close to a two-year high, which means markets expect wholesale fuel prices to continue rising in the coming weeks, according to Barchart data. Fuel prices have become a major political issue in the U.S. because higher costs affect everyday spending and affordability for millions of Americans. Rising fuel prices in the USRising fuel prices are also putting pressure on the administration of Donald Trump, as energy costs are often linked to political debates and election outcomes. The recent military strikes on Iran and Iran’s large-scale retaliation strategy have shaken global oil markets and raised fears about supply disruptions. Experts warn that these tensions could push fuel prices higher depending on how long the conflict continues.The latest data from AAA shows that diesel prices have now climbed to $4.17 per gallon as of early Thursday morning. This new price is much higher than $3.66 per gallon recorded at the same time last year, according to AAA data cited by Newsweek. However, diesel prices are still lower than the record average of $5.82 per gallon, which happened in summer 2022 after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Analysts say the rise in pump prices usually follows global oil price increases, but it often takes days or weeks before consumers fully feel the change.Global oil prices continue to climbGlobal oil benchmark Brent crude is currently trading at around $83 per barrel. Analysts warn that oil prices could climb above $100 per barrel, a level not seen since 2022, if shipping disruptions in the Gulf region continue. A key risk point is the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway where about one-fifth of the world’s oil supply passes through. Shipping in this vital route has been disrupted because of the conflict, which has slowed oil transport and worried global markets.Iran has carried out attacks across the Gulf that have also hit important energy facilities. Because of repeated drone attacks, several oil refineries have been forced to stop their operations, according to Newsweek. Torbjorn Soltvedt, a Middle East analyst at Verisk Maplecroft, said the situation is very serious because key energy facilities are now being directly targeted. Soltvedt explained that the global oil market is in a risky situation. Energy facilities are being attacked, and shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has almost stopped. He also warned that oil prices could continue to rise if the United States and Israel do not stop Iran from launching more drones and missiles.US plans steps to stabilize oil supplySoltvedt explained that oil supply problems have been limited so far because Gulf countries exported large amounts of oil earlier to prepare for possible conflict disruptions. However, he warned that this early export strategy will lose its effect in the coming weeks, which could make supply shortages worse, according to Soltvedt’s statement to Newsweek. He added that if Iranian attacks on Gulf energy sites and threats to shipping continue for two more weeks, oil prices reaching $100 per barrel could become a realistic possibility. President Donald Trump said during a Wednesday press conference that the U.S. was performing very well in the war effort. Trump said that if the situation was rated on a scale of 1 to 10, he would rate it “about a 15”. Analysts at Goldman Sachs warned that the ongoing oil price surge could also push inflation higher in the United States later this year. Higher oil prices usually increase transportation and production costs, which then raise prices for many goods and services across the economy.On Wednesday, Scott Bessent said the government was preparing a series of announcements about plans to support oil supply flows in the region. These steps are meant to reduce supply risks and stabilize energy markets during the ongoing Middle East conflict, according to Bessent’s statement cited by Newsweek. Earlier in the week, Trump also announced that the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation would offer political risk insurance and guarantees for maritime trade in the Gulf. The plan aims to protect ships and companies moving oil through the region during the conflict. Trump also said that if the situation becomes more dangerous, the United States Navy could escort oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz to keep global oil shipments moving safely. FAQsQ1. Why are diesel and gas prices rising in the United States?Fuel prices are rising because the Iran conflict has pushed global oil prices higher and disrupted supply routes like the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysts.Q2. Could oil prices reach $100 per barrel again?Yes, analysts say oil prices could cross $100 per barrel if attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping disruptions continue.",

			  "articleBody":"President Donald Trump told Axios in an exclusive Thursday interview that he must be personally involved in selecting Iran’s next leader, just as he was in Venezuela. The comments came during an eight-minute phone call, his second with the outlet to explain his war planning.Trump confirmed that Mojtaba Khamenei, the 56-year-old son of the assassinated supreme leader Ali Khamenei, is the most likely successor but said he finds this outcome unacceptable.He told Reuters that it is very early in the process of selecting Iran’s next leader and described Mojtaba Khamenei as unlikely to take the role. The president also expressed support for the Kurds launching an offensive into Iran, saying: “I think it’s wonderful if they want to do that.” He added that the Strait of Hormuz will be kept open, signalling a commitment to maintaining regional maritime security.On the economic front, Trump said gasoline prices have not risen much at this point despite the ongoing conflict. He also noted that the Iran operation is moving ahead of schedule but declined to provide a specific timeline.Trump highlighted the U.S. military’s preparedness, stating that the country has tremendous amounts of ammunition and that the defense industry is ramping up production, adding that there is no need to invoke the Defense Production Act.He added that he refuses to accept a new Iranian leader who would continue Khamenei’s policies, warning that such a scenario could force the U.S. back to war “in five years.”You can follow our live coverage of the Iran-Israel war here“They are wasting their time. Khamenei’s son is a lightweight. I have to be involved in the appointment, like with Delcy [Rodriguez] in Venezuela,” Trump said. “We want someone that will bring harmony and peace to Iran.”For several days, the Iranian regime has postponed announcing the new supreme leader, but statements by Iranian politicians on Thursday suggested an announcement could be imminent.Trump’s remarks represent an extraordinary claim of American influence over Iran’s political future, coming amid the massive U.S. military campaign launched on Saturday. While U.S. officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the operation aims for regime change, Trump’s statements further complicate understanding of the campaign’s objectives.The war in the Middle East entered its sixth day as Iran launched additional missiles at Israel and U.S. bases. Israel reported multiple incoming attacks early Thursday and said its defence systems were intercepting the missiles.Meanwhile, the Israeli military said it had launched new strikes against the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group in Lebanon. According to Lebanon’s Health Ministry and state news agencies, at least eight people were killed late Wednesday into Thursday during the attacks.Also Read: Trump wants a quick victory in Iran. But the war may be costly.Tehran has warned of the destruction of the region’s military and economic infrastructure. The conflict has also shaken global financial markets, with investors closely watching oil prices, which resumed their ascent early Thursday.Officials in the affected countries said the war has so far killed at least 1,230 people in Iran, more than 70 in Lebanon, and around a dozen in Israel, including six U.S. troops.",

“What Turns our World?”

By
Brooks B. Robinson, Ph.D.

Mar 5, 2026, 10:04 AM CST

Share

Purpose: This Analysis Brief returns to a favorite BlackEconomics.org topic: The Power of the media and how it shapes our mind and behavior. Knowing that most media operations are held hostage to advertising revenue, it stands to reason that without advertising revenue certain media operations would cease to exist. Therefore, the symbiotic relationship between the media and advertising ensures that the two collaborate to enforce a vice grip on our lives. Media spares no expense to keep us engaged so that it can secure the advertising revenue that enables the media’s survival.

Introduction
Our lives were flooded with several important and powerful events last week: The State of the Union Address; a media awards programs with an unfavorable illness-driven outburst; news about economic growth, stock market hiccups, and inflation; and a long-awaited but certain attack on the Muslim World. This represents a considerable amount of information to digest, but we were well prepared to receive it. Really? Yes! It was “advertised” well in advance. Rest assured that the purpose of almost all, if not all, media content is to advertise: i.e., to entertain minds so that they are ready to receive advertisements, or provide informational content that, at its root, is some form of advertisement.

This Analysis Brief is a reminder that our lives are governed largely by the media, and the media helps direct our activity through advertising. Our consumption and our actions are motivated in significant ways by advertising. The business and economic literatures are transparent concerning these points, and important contributions to these literatures indicate that advertising was commonplace as early as the 17th century.i

How Important is Advertising?
We became fixated on advertising last week for no apparent reason. We remembered our long-held intent to prove the outcomes discussed in the previous paragraph statistically using readily available data. However, we had not set aside time to undertake the research. A time window opened last week, we collected the data, and we present the results of our straightforward Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analyses that are not as bright and beautifully blue as the sky and ocean waters of Oahu appear, but they are sufficient to prove our hypotheses.

For those unfamiliar with such statistical analyses, please do not worry and do not feel excluded from the conversation. Bypass the technical symbolism and vernacular of econometrics. Focus on the analytical results, which are easily comprehended. “There is no rocket science but rocket science itself.” A little-known secret is that all economists are not equal. Economists are not licensed, so we are not held to the same qualifying standard. Each degree granting institution separately determines who is hooded. Therefore, certain economists have a constrained command of statistics, which may be greater, equal to, or less than your own.

Details (variable names, sources, characteristics, and expected arithmetic signs for the related regression model coefficients) concerning annual data that enter our regression analysis models are provided in Table 1 (page 3) . The variables of interest are: (1) Real business (not total) receipts (RBR) of US corporations; (2) the number of IRS 1120 tax returns (NOR) filed by corporate firms; (3) Real advertising expenditures (RAE) by corporate entities; and (4) the growth in real (chained dollars) gross domestic product (RGDP) during a year. Data for the models span 2001 – 2022 and all variables undergo natural logarithmic transformations for uniformity and statistical standards purposes.

As a preliminary test of a “Bayesian Prior” (i.e., that advertising reflects a time decay (distributed lag) process), we estimated the correlations between RBRt and RAEt and RBRt and RAEt-1 (see Table 2). The table reveals that the latter correlation reflects lower positivity than the former. Hence, our analytical models only concern simultaneous effects between RBRt and RAEt. In other words, we rejected our Bayesian Prior and concluded that, for this analysis, we would ignore the question of whether previous-period advertising impacts current-period receipts.

Equation (1) presents the core regression model that we estimate:

Equation 1:

Where α represents the estimated model coefficients (with α1t serving as a “constant” term), t is the time indicator (t and t-1), ln indicates a logarithmic transformation of the variables that were already identified, and ε represents the error term that is assumed to be randomly and identically distributed. For Model I, all the variables are considered. For Model II, the RGDP variable is excluded from the model for reasons to be explained below.

Results for Models I and II are presented in Tables 3 and 4 (pages 5 and 6). They reveal that these straightforward OLS statistical regression models reflect a high level of explanatory power. Specifically, the Adjusted R-Squares indicate that at least 83 percent of the variation in the RBR variable is explained by both models.

Also, and unsurprisingly, Models I and II (Tables 3 and 4) indicate that the elasticity of the relationship between RAE and RBR ranges from 0.39 percent and 0.37 percent, respectively. That is, at the margin, a one (1.0) percent increase in RAE is expected to be associated with a nearly 0.40 percent increase in RBR.

Importantly, we exclude the RGDP variable from Model II (Table 4) because its coefficient in Model I (Table 3) reflects an unexpected, but theoretically logical negative relationship with RBR.ii On the other hand, this unexpected result could indicate distortions in regression models caused by “multicollinearity.”iii A test of the correlation between RAE and RGDP yielded a correlation coefficient of .971, which signals high collinearity between the two variables.

Conclusion
In accordance with the results of our statistical analysis, we conclude that firms’ spending on advertising is effective in helping generate sales and thereby increases business receipts. As Black Americans, however, we should certainly not permit the analysis to conclude with the latter statement. We should continue with the analysis and consider the following important questions about the media and advertising:


•How much media do we consume (adults and youth)?iv
•How much advertising do we encounter when we consume media?
•Do we purposely prevent advertising from reaching our subconscious minds, where it can drive our spending behavior at an unconscious level?
•Do Black American entrepreneurs expend sufficiently on advertising to achieve optimal results?v
•Has media and its advertising imprisoned us in a cycle of earning to spend, so that we are unable to pause, contemplate, and develop and execute a life plan that produces a much higher and more favorable level of overall wellbeing?

The foregoing series of questions may operate as an internal barometer for measuring our wellbeing. However, our lives are enmeshed in a broader and wide-ranging US socioeconomic system. Hence, it is appropriate for us to consider the extent to which the entire society is driven by advertising.

Consider that:
1.Income and wealth are at the top of our hierarchy of needs.
2.To secure income and wealth, we work.
3.We enjoy employment opportunities because our public or private sector employers incur advertising costs to sell their products.
4.To sustain the American dream and mystique, the nation’s governments rely heavily on their spending power, which serves as a form of advertisement.
5.Although certain adherents of monetary economic theory may disagree, few Americans reject the notion that government spending is linked to tax revenue, and that tax revenue rises when economic growth increases.
6.Economic growth accelerates or is sustained when firms advertise to increase sales.

Because the results of our statistical analyses support the conclusion that our world turns on advertising, we now comprehend how we arrived at all the favorable or unfavorable outcomes identified in the first paragraph of this Analytical Brief.

Endnotes
i Charles Allen (1942). “The Press and Advertising.” The Annals of the American Academy of Political Science. Vol. 219. The Press in the Contemporary Scene. (January), pp. 86-92. https://www.jstor.org/stable/1023897 (Ret. 030226).
ii In certain cases, it is reasonable to expect that when the economy is growing at an elevated rate (a high growth rate for real GDP), firms may be motivated to reduce their advertising expenses. On the other hand, and the basis of our “Bayesian Prior,” economists often adopt the mantra: “More is better.” That is, if spending on advertising engenders higher receipts, then why halt or reduce that spending—even if receipts and the economy broadly are experiencing growth at an elevated rate?
iii Econometricians recognize the distorting effects of high multicollinearity on statistical results and act to eliminate it. The often-used remedy is to remove one of two highly correlated variables from the right-hand side of the regression equation.
iv The Bureau of Labor Statistics produces the American Time Use Survey (ATUS). It is common knowledge that the ATUS has a persistent record of reporting that Black Americans spend more time in an entertainment mode (Leisure and Sports) than any other racial/ethnic group in the US. (Ret. 030226)
v According to the Census Bureau’s Annual Business Survey for 2023, there were about 4.6 million Black American owned enterprise, but only about 200K were employer firms; the remainder were nonemployer firms. It could be that Black enterprises form in industries that are too competitive and do not offer opportunities to grow sufficiently to take on employees. It may also be the case that many of the nearly 4.0 million Black American owned nonemployer firms are operating as hobbies/side hustles; not as going concerns determined to optimize production, earnings, and profits/net income. However, it is also true that too many Black enterprises’ financial capital structure is inadequate to permit adequate advertising expenditures, which can help produce greater profitability and growth, and an opportunity to become employing firms. (Ret. 030226)
vi The following are few data points that may be of interest concerning spending on Advertising: (1) For the period 2001-2022, the average annual ratio of Advertising expense-to-Business Receipts and of Advertising expense-to-Total Deductions (expenses) reported on Form 1120 to the IRS was 1.15 percent and 1.07 percent, respectively; and (2) The total values for Business Receipts, Total Deductions, and Advertising expenses from Form 1120 filed with the IRS for tax year 2022 were $39.9 trillion, $41.3 trillion, and $473.2 billion, respectively.
vii The following are URLs where the statistics used in this analysis can be identified (Ret. 022726):
BEA: https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey (NIPA Table 1..6.—Real Gross Domestic Product, Chained Dollars)
BLS: https://www.bls.gov/cpi/
FRED: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/
SOI: https://www.irs.gov/statistics/soi-tax-stats-corporation-tax-statistics (Table 2.1. Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and Selected Items, by Size of Total Assets; and Table 27. Balance Sheet, Income Statement, including Investment Data, by Selected Sectors).

Brooks B. Robinson, Ph.D. / Milwaukee Courier

  <div class="grid-ten large-grid-nine grid-last content-body content entry-content instapaper_body inline-promos" itemprop="articleBody">
    <p>France’s vision of universal healthcare and America’s health insurance premium-reliant system are worlds apart. On October 1 2025, the US Federal Government <a href="https://theconversation.com/how-the-government-shutdown-is-hitting-the-health-care-system-and-what-the-battle-over-aca-subsidies-means-266565">shut down</a> after an insufficient number of Democrat votes amid disputes over health policy led to a federal government budget deadlock</p>

<p><a href="https://www.axios.com/2025/11/05/government-shutdown-length-days-record-trump">The longest shutdown in US history</a> could have had dramatic consequences for part of the population, particularly for millions of Americans who would have lost their health insurance. President Trump is on a mission to dismantle policies introduced by Barack Obama (and maintained under the Biden administration) to improve access to health insurance for the most <a href="https://theconversation.com/why-medicaid-matters-to-you-82122">disadvantaged</a>.</p>

<p>On top of the anticipated decline is the incredibly questionable policy of US Secretary of State for Health, <a href="https://www.lemonde.fr/en/health/article/2025/08/06/rfk-jr-pulls-500-million-in-funding-for-vaccine-development_6744108_14.html">Robert Francis Kennedy Jr</a>, and his highly controversial views on vaccines.</p>

<p>Meanwhile, despite a 17.5 billion deficit and a need for reform, in terms of quality and access to medical care, France’s <a href="https://www.ameli.fr/assure"><em>Assurance Maladie</em></a> national healthcare system remains a “land of plenty”.</p>

<h2>Efficient medical care, ‘<em>à la française</em>’</h2>

<p>A good starting point for explaining <a href="https://www.fabfrenchinsurance.com/health/understanding-the-french-healthcare-system-101-a-guide-for-expats/">France’s national health service</a> to Americans would be to step back in time.</p>

<p>In 1939, a US citizen’s life expectancy at birth was seven years higher than for a French citizen. Things have changed since then. In 2024, it was more than three and a half years lower: <a href="https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db548.htm">life expectancy stood at 79</a> in the United States compared to <a href="https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/2416631">82.5</a> in France. In 2025, however, healthcare expenditure per capita was equivalent to <a href="https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/health-at-a-glance-2025_8f9e3f98-en/full-report/health-expenditure-per-capita_affe6b0a.html">12,627 euros</a> in the United States (14,885 dollars), and <a href="https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/health-at-a-glance-2025_8f9e3f98-en/full-report/health-expenditure-per-capita_affe6b0a.html">6,249 euros</a> in France (7,367 dollars).</p><div class="slot clear" data-id="17">
<div class="inline-promos-skeleton">
  <h5></h5>
  <button></button>
</div>
</div>

<p>At national level, this translates into so-called health costs (mainly medical fees), representing <a href="https://drees.solidarites-sante.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2025-09/CNS--Fiche26--Comparaisonsinternationalesdelad%C3%A9pensecourantedesant%C3%A9en2023et2024_0.pdf">17.2%</a> of GDP in the US and <a href="https://drees.solidarites-sante.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2025-09/CNS--Fiche26--Comparaisonsinternationalesdelad%C3%A9pensecourantedesant%C3%A9en2023et2024_0.pdf">11.4%</a> in France. While changes in life expectancy are linked to lifestyle and eating habits (leading to <a href="https://theconversation.com/weight-loss-drug-stigma-shows-society-still-holds-negative-attitudes-towards-body-weight-and-obesity-265019">obesity</a> and <a href="https://beta.ncdpolicylab.org/resources/research-articles/acces-a-linsuline-les-roles-des-gouvernements">diabetes)</a>, the effectiveness of medicine is playing an increasingly important role.</p>

<p>It is likely that the quality of healthcare for the majority of people is both better and more accessible in France.</p>

<p>When it comes to paying for medical care, France has a simple system: it is a country where you are covered by health insurance from birth. All legal residents are automatically registered with the health insurance system and, therefore, receive free healthcare for the most serious conditions, or care that is largely reimbursed within the compulsory health insurance scheme and covered by top-up insurance plans.</p>

<p>In the US, there is a three-tier social security system: <a href="https://www.medicare.gov/">Medicare</a> for the over 65s and people with disabilities, <a href="https://www.medicaid.gov/">Medicaid</a> for the poorest, and the <a href="https://www.va.gov/health/">Veterans Health Administration</a> for veterans.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">

<h2>7.8% out-of-pocket expenses for French citizens</h2>

<p><a href="https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F34068">Thirty long-term serious conditions</a> such as cancer, type 1 or 2 diabetes or psychiatric illnesses are fully covered (treatment is fully reimbursed) by the compulsory state health cover that is offered to all French citizens.</p>

<p>If we add top-up health insurance – now <a href="https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2019-11/2019_companion_en_0.pdf">almost</a> universal – patients in France actually only end up paying 7.8% of their healthcare costs. Admittedly, French citizens or their employers will have contributed in financing compulsory or top-up health insurance.</p>

<p>For most French people, there are few or no financial barriers to entry. These barriers have been further reduced for dental care, optical care and hearing care thanks to a universal policy implemented by Emmanuel Macron called <a href="https://drees.solidarites-sante.gouv.fr/publications-en-anglais/250603_ER_100-sante-reform-france-expected-effects-premiums-private-complementary">“100% healthcare”</a>.</p>

<p>On the whole the French system is more generous than those of comparable countries.</p>

<p>Patients are encouraged to register with a general practitioner with whom visits are then fully reimbursed. If they choose to consult a different health professional, it will only cost them a few euros more. Patients are can make same day appointments to see several specialists whose fees are largely reimbursed, that is unless they don’t charge rates higher than those set by the National Health Service (known as “excess fees”), a common practice in certain medical specialities.</p>

<h2>France: a predominantly state-run health service</h2>

<p>Like in the United States, France has public hospitals, private clinics and private non-profit clinics. All 31 of France’s university hospitals are state-funded.</p>

<p>France does, however have a higher percentage of private (for-profit) hospitals than the United States. In 2024, 33% of clinics in France were private compared to 20% in the <a href="https://www.aha.org/statistics/fast-facts-us-hospitals">US</a>.</p>

<p>In France, private practice physicians are free to set up practice wherever they wish and are paid on a fee-for-service basis. In the majority of cases, doctors’ fees are set by the national health insurance system and are much lower than in the United States: 30 euros for a visit with a general practitioner in France, <a href="https://www.jean-jaures.org/publication/systemes-de-sante-une-comparaison-france-etats-unis/">$150</a> in the United States, or 127 euros.</p>

<h2>Strong French state regulation</h2>

<p>It goes without saying that in France, the State is heavily involved in regulating its national health service.</p>

<p>Opening a pharmacy is impossible without administrative authorisation, for instance. The State, through its regional health agencies, controls all hospitals – public or private. It manages the register for all medical procedures, pricing and reimbursement rates for each medicine, X-ray or biological test a doctor prescribes. At national level, the State is responsible for appointing all directors and doctors in public hospitals, which employed nearly 1.1 million people at the end of 2021.</p>

<p>High-quality private establishments are present in France (<a href="https://drees.solidarites-sante.gouv.fr/publications-communique-de-presse/en-2022-nine-out-of-ten-private-clinics-are-part-of-a-group">they employed 315,000 people in 2022</a> and, I would again lay emphasis on how private doctors are free to set up their own practices and prescribe care as they see fit.</p>

<p>Despite everything, the French system is one of the most expensive in the Western world. Hospital stays account for a large proportion of expenditure. France has many specialists, and medication consumption is high.</p>

<p>The<a href="https://www.kff.org/health-costs/health-policy-101-health-care-costs-and-affordability/?entry=table-of-contents-what-factors-contribute-to-u-s-health-care-spending#xd_co_f=MDA4YWNkZDUtYjIwNy00NjQzLTljYmYtNDIxY2U2YzlkMWU1%7E">American system</a> is is even more expensive, and, in reality, more <a href="https://www.hematologyadvisor.com/news/many-americans-say-u-s-health-care-is-in-trouble-poll-finds/">inefficient</a> because competition between private insurers does not lead to a reduction in the cost of services – as is often the case in a market economy – it results in <a href="https://kffhealthnews.org/news/article/insurers-pay-high-prices-premiums-coinsurance-cost-control-inflation-patients/">inflation</a> in insurance premiums. Backed firmly by their belief in the absolute and systematic benefits of all forms of competition, wealthy individuals in the United States take out insurance policies to cover the fees of renowned doctors and stays in luxury hospitals. In doing so, they ramp up the costs of medical goods and services.</p>

<h2>The US healthcare system is, in essence, ‘inflationary’</h2>

<p>Over time, US healthcare providers’ tariffs (having been made solvent by part of the demand) have increased, leading to inflation. The high expenditure of the US health service, which is an inherently inflationary system, compared to other Western countries, is mainly due to a difference in the pricing of medical goods and healthcare professionals’ fees.</p>

<p>The reforms during Barack Obama’s term in office did nothing to curb this inflation. Donald Trump <a href="https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/12/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-announces-largest-developments-to-date-in-bringing-most-favored-nation-pricing-to-american-patients/">says</a> he wants to tackle this by putting pressure on drug prices in particular.</p>

<p>It is plain to see that universal health insurance allows for operational control over medical and hospital fees and the price of prescription drugs. This is the norm in OECD countries, such as France. This does not mean that doctors or nurses are poorly paid, or that there is no access to medical breakthroughs, but rather that regulation is safeguarded, i.e. not left to a market which, in the specific case of healthcare, mainly produces inflation.</p>

<h2>Are the United States more socialist?</h2>

<p>To conclude with a brief arithmetic demonstration: public health expenditure, financed by taxes and compulsory contributions, represents <a href="https://www.healthsystemtracker.org/chart-collection/u-s-spending-healthcare-changed-time/#Total%20national%20spending%20on%20health%20consumption%20expenditures,%20$U.S.%20billions,%20by%20payer,%202024">43%</a> of healthcare expenditure in the US, or <a href="https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/health-at-a-glance-2025_8f9e3f98-en/full-report/health-expenditure-per-capita_affe6b0a.html">4,532 euros</a> per capita per year (43% of the 10,517 euros in current healthcare expenses). In France, these expenses represent 79.4% or <a href="https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/health-at-a-glance-2025_15a55280-en/france_fea63dd5-en.html">4,195 euros</a> or 4,863 dollars – 79.4% of 5,273 euros in current healthcare expenses per person per year, with the remainder being covered by patients themselves or their top-up health insurance plans.</p>

<p>In other words, US taxes provide more funding for the healthcare system in absolute terms! Can we safely say that this makes the United States more “socialist” in its approach? Obviously, there is no supporting evidence to suggest this, but it is clear that Americans pay twice for their healthcare: once through their taxes and a second time via their insurance premiums.</p>

<p>People in the US have long been aware of this and have become staunch supporters of <a href="https://kffhealthnews.org/news/kennedy-health-care-timeline/">universal health insurance, introduced by the late Senator Ted Kennedy</a>, the youngest of the Kennedy brothers. The chances of such a reform making it onto the political agenda in the short term are nil because, to conclude with a quote from Marcel Proust’s <em>Swann’s Way</em>:</p>

<blockquote>
<p>“The facts of life do not penetrate the sphere in which our beliefs are cherished; as it was not they that engendered those beliefs, so they are powerless to destroy them.”</p>
</blockquote>

<p>Beliefs in the universal efficiency of the market are therefore as firm as they are costly, and are now more alive than ever.</p>

	function findParentByTagName(element, name) {
		var parent = element.parentElement
		if(!parent || !parent.tagName) {
			return false
		}
		if(parent.tagName.toLowerCase() == name.toLowerCase()) {
			return parent
		}
		return findParentByTagName(parent, name)

	function closeDialog() {
		for(const closer of document.querySelectorAll("fluent-dialog .dialog-closer")) {
			try {
				closer.addEventListener("click", () => {
					try {
						var p = findParentByTagName(closer, "fluent-dialog")

							p.closeDialog()

					}

			}
		}
	}
	
	window.sendDCMessage = function(origin, name, args) {
		try {
			parent.postMessage({
				name: name,
				args: args
			}, origin || "*"); // TODO remove * after testing
		} catch(e) {
			console.error("[sendDCMessage] Failed to send message:", e);
		}
	}
	
	window.generateSelector = function(element){
		if (!element || !element.parentElement) {
			return '';
		}
		
		element = element.parentElement;
		
		if (element.tagName === 'HTML' || element.tagName === 'BODY') {
			return element.tagName.toLowerCase();
		}
		
		let selector = element.tagName.toLowerCase();
		
		if (element.parentElement) {
			const siblings = Array.from(element.parentElement.children);
			const index = siblings.indexOf(element);
			if (siblings.filter(s => s.tagName === element.tagName).length > 1) {
				selector += `:nth-child(${index + 1})`;
			}
		}
		
		const parentSelector = window.generateSelector(element);
		
		if (parentSelector === 'body' || parentSelector === 'html') {
			return selector;
		}
		
		return parentSelector ? `${parentSelector} > ${selector}` : selector;
	}
	
	var setupTemplate = async (template) => {
		console.log("[setupTemplate] Setting up template", template)
	
		template.allowNextSetup = () => {
			if(Object.keys(template).includes("alreadySetup")) {
				delete template.alreadySetup
			}
		}
	
		if(template.alreadySetup) {
			console.warn("[setupTemplate] Template already setup, skipping...", template)
			return
		}
	
		const checkSetup = async () => {
			if(template.setup) {
				console.warn("[setupTemplate] Setup function found for template, calling...", template)
				template.alreadySetup = true
				template.setup()
			} else {
				console.warn("[setupTemplate] No setup function found for template, waiting 100ms and retrying...", template.setup)
				await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 100))
				await checkSetup()
			}
		}
		
		await checkSetup()
	}

	window.showDCTemplate = function(origin, name) {
		var template = document.querySelector(`.${name}`)
		if(!template) {
			console.error("[showDCTemplate] Unable to find template", name)
			return false
		}
		template.style.removeProperty("display")

			const fluentCard = document.createElement("fluent-card")
			for (const attr of template.attributes) {

			}
			fluentCard.closeDialog = template.closeDialog
			fluentCard.setup = template.setup
			delete template.setup
			fluentCard.innerHTML = template.innerHTML
			fluentCard.original = template
			template.remove()

		}
		try {
			template.show()
		} catch(e) {
			template.style.display = "block"
			template.style.removeProperty("display")
		}
		templateCommon(origin, name, template)
		setupTemplate(template)
	}
	
	window.injectDCTemplate = function(origin, name, selector){
		var template = document.querySelector(`.${name}`)
		if(!template){
			if(!window.dcTemplatesReady) {
				console.log("[injectDCTemplate] Waiting on template", name)
				document.addEventListener("DCTemplateReady", () => {
					injectDCTemplate(origin, name, selector)
				})
			} else {
				console.error("[injectDCTemplate] Unable to find template", name)
			}
			return false
		}
		template.removeAttribute("style")
		var target = document.querySelector(selector)
		if(!target){
			console.error("[injectDCTemplate] unable to find target",selector)
			return false
		}
		target.appendChild(template)
		template.removeAttribute('modal')
		const positioningRegion = template.shadowRoot?.children[0];
		if (positioningRegion?.classList.contains('positioning-region')) {
			positioningRegion.style.position = 'relative';
		}
		template.style.display = "inherit"
	
		templateCommon(origin, name, template)
		setupTemplate(template)
	}

	// Add the viewability tracker function for paywalls
	// *************************************************
	function setupViewabilityTracker(selector, eventName) {
		// Special handling for stream-subscribe-template (video paywall)
		if (selector === '.stream-subscribe-template') {
			const dialog = document.querySelector('fluent-dialog.stream-subscribe-template');
			if (!dialog) {
				console.warn(`[template-init] Fluent dialog not found: ${selector}`);
				return;
			}
	
			// Function to handle dialog becoming visible
			const handleDialogShow = (dialog) => {
				if (!dialog.hasAttribute('hidden') && !dialog.dataset.eventFired) {
					setTimeout(() => {
						// Double check still visible and not fired
						if (!dialog.hasAttribute('hidden') && !dialog.dataset.eventFired) {
							dialog.dataset.eventFired = 'true';
							if (rudderanalytics && rudderanalytics.track) {
								rudderanalytics.track(eventName, window.dcRudderstack);
							} else {
								console.error(`[template-init] Failed to track dialog - rudderanalytics not available`);
							}
						}
					}, 1000);
				}
			};
	
			// Watch for hidden attribute changes
			const dialogObserver = new MutationObserver((mutations) => {
				mutations.forEach((mutation) => {
					if (mutation.attributeName === 'hidden') {
						handleDialogShow(mutation.target);
					}
				});
			});
	
			// Start observing the dialog
			dialogObserver.observe(dialog, {
				attributes: true,
				attributeFilter: ['hidden']
			});
			// Check initial state (in case dialog is already visible)
			handleDialogShow(dialog);
			
			return;
		}
		
		// Intersection observer for regwall and paywall
		const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
			entries.forEach(entry => {
				const element = entry.target;
				if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.intersectionRatio >= 0.5 && !element.dataset.eventFired) {
					setTimeout(() => {
						if (entry.isIntersecting && !element.dataset.eventFired) {
							element.dataset.eventFired = 'true';
							if (rudderanalytics && rudderanalytics.track) {
								rudderanalytics.track(eventName, window.dcRudderstack);
							} else {
								console.error(`[template-init] Failed to track - rudderanalytics not available`);
							}
							
							observer.unobserve(element);
						}
					}, 1000);
				}
			});
		}, {
			threshold: 0.5
		});
		
		const element = document.querySelector(selector);
		if (element) {
			observer.observe(element);
		} else {
			console.warn(`[template-init] Element not found: ${selector}`);
		}
	}

		const checkPaywall = async () => {
			const pats = window.dc_targeting.dccategories.includes("premium-content")
	
			if(pats && window.dc.premiumcontent) {
				const res = await SupabaseClient.functions.invoke('fetchArticle', {
					body: {
						articlePath: window.location.pathname
					}
				})
				if(res.error) {
					console.error("[checkPaywall] error fetching article", res.error)
					return
				}
	
				try {
					const feed = JSON.parse(res.data)
					const article = feed.item.encoded.__text
					const node = new DOMParser().parseFromString(article, "text/html").querySelector("#ob-read-more-selector")
					if(node) {
						document.querySelector("#ob-read-more-selector").replaceWith(node)
					} else {
						throw new Error("No node found in article")
					}
				} catch(e) {
					console.error("[checkPaywall] error parsing article", e)
					return
				}
			} else if(pats) {
				showPaywall()
				return
			} else if(window.dc.premiumcontent) {
				return
			} else {
				/* Dynamic Paywall */
				try {
					const cookie = ( () => {
						try {
							return document.cookie.split("; ")
							               .find((c) => c.startsWith("_dc_pw"))
							               .split("=")[1]
						} catch(e) {
							return ""
						}
					} )()
					const p = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
					const utm_action = p ? p.get('utm_action') : ""
	
					if(cookie == "true" || utm_action == "paywall") {
						/* One month */
						var expiration = new Date(Date.now() + 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30).toUTCString()
						document.cookie = `_dc_pw=true; path=${document.location.pathname}; expires=${expiration}`
						dc_track("Show Paywall")
						showPaywall()
						return
					}
				} catch(e) {
					console.error("[Dynamic Paywall]", e)
					/* pass */
				}
			}
	
		}

		function dc_track(e, da = {}) {
			const payload = { ...da }
			if(window.dcRudderstack) {
				for(const key in window.dcRudderstack) {
					payload[key] = window.dcRudderstack[key]
				}
			}
			window.marfeel = window.marfeel || { cmd: [] };
			if(window.marfeel){
				window.marfeel.cmd.push(['compass', function(compass) {
					console.log("[dc_track] tracking conversion for Marfeel", e)
					compass.trackConversion(e);
				}]);
			}
			return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
				if(rudderanalytics && rudderanalytics.page) {
					rudderanalytics.track(e, payload, window.dcRudderstackContext);
					setTimeout(() => {
						resolve()
					}, 1000)
				} else {
					console.warn("[dc_track] rudderanalytics is not ready")
					resolve()
				}
			})
		}

		window.dc_lastReceivedUser = undefined
		const authStateChangeListener = async (event, session) => {
			if(session?.user?.id) {
				if(window.dc_lastReceivedUser === session.user.id) {
					return
				}
				window.dc_lastReceivedUser = session.user.id
			}
	
			try {
				if(event === "SIGNED_IN" || (event === "INITIAL_SESSION" && session)) {
					var userEmail = session.user.email
					var userID = session.user.id
					var accessToken = session.access_token
					var userdata = {
						email: userEmail,
						firstname: "",
						lastname: "",
						uid: userID,
						oldtoken: accessToken
					}
	
					await dc_identify(userdata)
					document.dispatchEvent(new Event("DCAccountsReady"))
					window.dcAccountsReady = true
				} else if(event === "SIGNED_OUT" || (event === "INITIAL_SESSION" && !session)) {
					window.dc_lastReceivedUser = undefined
					await dc_unidentify()
					document.dispatchEvent(new Event("DCAccountsReady"))
					window.dcAccountsReady = true
				}
			} catch(e) {
				console.error("[onAuthStateChange] Error checking session", e)
				await dc_unidentify()
				document.dispatchEvent(new Event("DCAccountsReady"))
				window.dcAccountsReady = true
			}
		}

		function dc_create_test(args = {}) {
			const required_args = {
				states: true,
				makeChanges: true,
				setupConversions: true,
				name: true
			}
			Object.keys(required_args).forEach(function(arg) {
				if(-1 == Object.keys(args).indexOf(arg)) {
					console.error(`[dc_create_test] Missing argument: ${arg}, exiting.`);
					return;
				}
			});
	
			function genRandomNum(num){
				var newNum = Math.floor(Math.random() * num);
				return newNum;
			}
	
			if(!Array.isArray(args.states) || args.states.length < 1) {
				console.error(`[dc_create_test] states must be non-empty array, exiting.`);
				return
			}
	
			const versionResult = args.states[genRandomNum(args.states.length)];
	
			gtag('event', `${args.name}: Impression`, {
				'event_category': "Testing",
				'event_label': versionResult,
				'send_to': 'G-B906X4P4C5',
				'non_interaction': true,
				'transport': 'beacon'
			});
	
			try {
				args.setupConversions(function(ev) {
					gtag('event', `${args.name}: Conversion`, {
						'event_category': "Testing",
						'event_label': versionResult,
						'send_to': 'G-B906X4P4C5',
						'non_interaction': false,
						'transport': 'beacon'
					});
				});
			} catch(e) {
				console.error(`[dc_create_test] Whoops, failed in setupConversions`, e);
			}
	
			try {
				args.makeChanges(versionResult);
			} catch(e) {
				console.error(`[dc_create_test] Whoops, failed in makeChanges`, e);
			}
		}

Iran is pummeled by airstrikes as it launches a new wave of attacks against Israel and US bases

By Associated Press
March 5, 2026
Share

Related

  • Iran is pummeled by airstrikes as it launches a new wave of attacks against Israel and US bases
  • Last 2 names of 6 US soldiers who died in Kuwait attack identified by the Pentagon
  • Senate Republicans vote down legislation to halt Iran attack in Congress’ first vote on the conflict

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Iran launched a new wave of attacks against Israel, American bases and countries around the region Thursday, while warning the U.S. would “bitterly regret” torpedoing an Iranian warship. Tehran’s expanding retaliatory strikes came even as Israel and the U.S. hammered Iran for a sixth day.

The war has escalated each day, affecting an additional 14 countries across the Middle East and beyond. On Thursday, Azerbaijan accused Iran of attacking it with drones — though Tehran denied that. A day earlier, the U.S. said it sank an Iranian frigate in the waters off Sri Lanka.

Israel meanwhile issued a mass evacuation warning for all of Beirut’s southern suburbs as the fighting escalated with Lebanon’s Iran-allied Hezbollah militants. U.N. peacekeepers reported ground combat in southern Lebanon as more Israeli troops crossed the border.

All the while, the U.S. and Israel have battered Iran with nationwide strikes, targeting their military capabilities, leadership and nuclear program. Israeli and American leaders have also suggested that toppling the government was a goal — and Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed when they launched the war Saturday. But the exact aims and timelines have repeatedly shifted, and the conflict increasingly appeared to be open-ended.

U.S. President Donald Trump has told Axios on Thursday that he should be involved in picking Iran’s next supreme leader, and that Mojtaba Khamenei, a frontrunner to succeed his father, would be an “unacceptable” choice.

Iran’s attacks have targeted their Arab neighbors, disrupted oil supplies and snarled global air travel.

The war has killed at least 1,230 people in Iran, more than 100 in Lebanon and around a dozen in Israel, according to officials in those countries. Six U.S. troops have been killed.

Iran remains defiant

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the U.S. Navy of committing an “an atrocity at sea” for sinking the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean earlier in the week, killing at least 87 people.

“Mark my words: The U.S. will come to bitterly regret (the) precedent it has set,” he said on social media.

An Iranian cleric later called on state television for the shedding of both Israeli and “Trump’s blood.”

The statement from Ayatollah Abdollah Javadi Amoli represented a rare call for violence by an ayatollah, one of the highest ranks within the clergy of Shiite Islam. There are dozens in Iran.

The war keeps expanding

Israel announced multiple incoming missile attacks and air sirens sounded in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem. The Israeli military said it carried out a wave of strikes on Iran’s ballistic missile launch sites.

Gulf countries also reported coming under fire. In the United Arab Emirates, a drone was shot down near the Al Dhafra Air Base, which hosts U.S. forces, and shrapnel fell to the ground, authorities said. Six people were wounded.

Qatar evacuated residents near the U.S. Embassy in Doha as a temporary precaution and later reported a missile attack on the city. Saudi Arabia said it destroyed a drone in its province bordering Jordan. Sirens sounded in Bahrain Thursday afternoon, while the country’s Defense Ministry said its forces had intercepted 75 Iranian ballistic missiles and 124 drones since the start of the war on Saturday.

Bahrain says an Iranian missile hit a state-run oil refinery. It said the fire Thursday night was extinguished and the refinery was still working. There were no reports of casualties.

Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev accused Iran of carrying out “a groundless act of terror and aggression” after a drone crashed Thursday near the airport in Nakhchivan, a region bordering Iran that is separated from the rest of the country by Armenia. Another drone fell near a school. Azerbaijan’s Prosecutor General’s office said four civilians, all airport workers, were wounded.

Aliyev said the military had been instructed “to prepare and implement retaliatory measures.”

Iran’s general staff of the armed forces denied it had launched drones toward Azerbaijan. Iran has also repeatedly denied targeting oil infrastructure and other civilian targets, even as its missiles and drones have hit such sites.

A tanker apparently came under attack off the coast of Kuwait early Thursday, expanding the area where commercial shipping was in danger, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center run by the British military. It said there was an explosion but did not offer a cause.

Since the war began Saturday, ships have been attacked in the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world’s oil is shipped. That has caused oil prices to soar.

Israel issues evacuation warning for Beirut suburbs

Israel issued an evacuation notice calling for all residents of Beirut’s southern suburbs to “save your lives and evacuate your homes immediately,” apparently signaling plans for heavy bombardment of the area.

Since the resurgence of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah, which struck Israel in the opening days of the war, Israel has hit sites in Beirut’s suburbs and issued a blanket warning for residents of southern Lebanon to evacuate.

Among the 80 targets in Lebanon the Israel military said it hit over the past 24 hours were “several command centers” used by Hezbollah in Beirut. It showed video footage of a building being hit, but provided no further details.

A spokesperson for the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon said on Thursday that peacekeepers had seen and heard clashes, including ground combat, in southern Lebanon as more Israeli forces have moved across the border.

“Ground combat was observed west of Kfar Kila,” a village near the border with Israel, overnight, UNIFIL spokesperson Tilak Pokharel said. Peacekeepers also saw “air attacks and flares and heard explosions” in the town of Khiyam, about five kilometers (three miles) from the border.

Iranian warship was hit on its way home from multinational exercises

The Iranian ship sunk by the U.S. Navy was returning from an exercise hosted by the Indian navy that the U.S. also joined.

Sri Lankan authorities said 32 crew members were rescued, while its navy recovered at least 87 bodies.

Araghchi said it had been carrying “almost 130” crew.

Sri Lanka’s media minister and government spokesman, Nalinda Jayatissa, told parliament Thursday that another Iranian ship had arrived in its waters. Jayatissa did not provide further details about the ship.

IMF warns of repercussions of conflict in Middle East on global economy

Published: 05 Mar 2026 - 06:58 pm | Last Updated: 05 Mar 2026 - 07:12 pm

Follow usnews
A+ A-
QNA

Bangkok: The Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), warned of the repercussions of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East on the global economy.

Global economic resilience has been tested yet again by the new conflict in the Middle East, said Kristalina Georgieva at the Asia in 2050 Conference in Bangkok.

"This conflict, if it proves to be more prolonged, has obvious potential to affect global energy prices, market sentiment, growth, and inflation, placing new demands on policymakers," she added.

Underscoring uncertainty is the new normal, Georgieva warned that new shocks in different shapes and sizes will keep coming.

For most of Asia, what is at stake is energy security and, through that, confidence, said Georgieva, noting that stock markets are already reacting.

IMF, as guardian of international economic and financial stability, is watching the events unfold very carefully, she said, adding that the IMF is assessing and quantifying the regional and global economic ramifications.

<article data-history-node-id="294159" role="article" about="/blogs/business/joseph-vazquez/2026/03/05/depaul-university-launches-new-racial-justice-anti-ice" class="node node--type-blog node--view-mode-full clearfix">
  <header>
    
          
        </header>
  <div class="node__content clearfix">
    
            <div class="field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item">
                        <p>Attention DePaul University donors! Do you want to check out how your funding is being put to use? The institution just initiated an obnoxious, new anti-ICE journalism institute in partnership with radical ex-Mayor of Chicago Lori Lightfoot and another Chicago-based left-wing group financed by some of the most notorious leftists in American politics.</p>

<p><img alt="" class="image-blog_image_50_ img-fluid blog-img" data-insert-attach="{"id":"d6a278ed-cded-4698-bafb-12c2533d5b4e","attributes":{"alt":["alt","description"],"title":["title"]}}" data-insert-class="image-blog_image_50_" data-insert-type="image" height="261" src="https://cdn.newsbusters.org/styles/blog_image_50_/s3/2026-03/Screenshot%202026-03-04%20142113.png?itok=lfg-leBQ" title="" width="465" /> The supposedly Catholic DePaul — which sits comfortably on a roughly <a href="https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/nacubo1-nacubo-prd-dc8b/media/Nacubo/Documents/EndowmentFiles/2025-NCSE-Endowment-Market-Values-for-US-and-Canadian-Institutions-FINAL.xlsx">$1.15 billion endowment</a> — announced that it was launching the cringely-named Institute for Journalism and Racial Justice (IJRJ) during a February 25 campus event, <a href="https://depauliaonline.com/83202/ladepaulia/depaul-launches-new-journalism-institute-aligned-with-lightfoot-ice-initiative/">according</a> to student newspaper <em>The DePaulia.</em></p>

<p>The announcement came following a “community briefing for a new Immigration and Customs Enforcement <strong>accountability platform</strong> led by” Lightfoot. Who held Lightfoot accountable? The Firearm Industry Trade Association <a href="https://www.nssf.org/articles/ousted-mayor-lightfoots-sudden-crime-amnesia/">panned</a> Lightfoot's tenure as Mayor in 2023 as being tainted by some of “the worst criminal and gang violence in memory.” Chicagoans <a href="https://www.illinoispolicy.org/chicago-homicides-in-2022-up-43-above-pre-pandemic-levels/">reported</a> a 43 percent crime increase in 2022 above pre-pandemic levels under her administration. But apparently, DePaul sees the former Democrat mayor as its guiding “Lightfoot.”</p>

<p><strong> “DePaul launches new journalism institute aligned with Lightfoot ICE initiative,</strong>” read the headline by <em>DePaulia </em>editor-in-chief Sofia Joseph and content managing editor Laura Vázquez David. Also telling was that the anti-ICE “community briefing” with Lightfoot was moderated by former ABC News <em>Nightline </em>correspondent <a href="https://www.depaul.edu/faculty/chris-bury">Chris Bury</a>, who has since become the senior journalist-in-residence at DePaul. Per <em>The Depaulia</em>, “In describing how racial justice comes into play at [her] ICE accountability project, Lightfoot” told Bury that “it is ‘fundamentally a part of where we are.’” </p>

<p>In keeping with Lightfoot’s distorted vision, one of the new Depaul institute’s <a href="https://communication.depaul.edu/academics/initiatives/institute-for-journalism-and-racial-justice">core goals</a> is to “[a]dvance racial justice in media by creating space for dialogue, learning and action that <strong>challenges inequitable media practices and promotes narrative change by employing asset-framing, solutions journalism and other innovative journalism practices towards more inclusive storytelling</strong>.” </p>

<p>Newsflash (no pun intended): Injecting leftist "racial justice" politics into storytelling is a textbook case of manufacturing propaganda, not journalism. </p>

<div class="video-embed-field-provider-youtube video-embed-field-responsive-video"><iframe width="854" height="480" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/XtKG7Ymyu4g?autoplay=0&start=0&rel=0"></iframe>
</div>


<p>Despite the fact that Chicago has become part of the nexus of criminal violence and <a href="https://www.newsbusters.org/blogs/nb/tim-graham/2026/02/06/column-pollsters-dont-ask-if-anti-ice-protesters-have-gone-too-far">resistance</a> against ICE officers carrying out federal immigration law, it appears that the IJRJ’s focus is to invert the perspective among student journalists to cast law enforcement as the aggressors and the criminals as the marginalized victims. Lightfoot’s adjoined <a href="https://reporticenow.com/about">anti-ICE initiative</a> states this plainly:</p>

<blockquote class="im--blockquote">
<p>Our purpose is to document and provide transparency to the public and other interested parties of the numerous allegations of serious misconduct committed by <strong>federal immigration agents who have been rampaging through our communities</strong> since the start of the so-called ‘Operation Midway Blitz’ in September, 2025. We aim to serve as a permanent, centralized repository to memorialize the information and evidence of the actions of the array of federal immigration agents operating in the towns and neighborhoods throughout Chicagoland since September 2025.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>"Rampaging?" Oh please. On November 9 2025, Department of Homeland Security Assistant Secretary Tricia McLaughlin <a href="https://www.dhs.gov/news/2025/11/09/border-patrol-agents-face-shots-fired-vehicle-rammings-bricks-thrown-chicago">stated</a> unequivocally that “Border Patrol faced gunshots, violent mobs at every stop, bricks and other objects thrown at them, and four vehicle rammings” in Chicago alone.</p>

<p>“The violence in Chicago against law enforcement is unprecedented—These attacks are the consequence of vitriolic smears from sanctuary politicians and the media,” McLaughlin continued. “Just last week, Chicago and national media falsely accused law enforcement of raiding a daycare center. Now, they are silent when our agents come under gunfire.” Who is it here that is "rampaging"?</p>

<p>Will DePaul University’s new “racial justice” journalism institute “aligned” with Lightfoot’s soft-on-crime radicalism change that trend? Doubtful.</p>

<p><img alt="" class="image-blog_image_100_ img-fluid blog-img" data-insert-attach="{"id":"868b6fa3-f9d1-4d8e-b7bc-38e10d97ab6c","attributes":{"alt":["alt","description"],"title":["title"]}}" data-insert-class="image-blog_image_100_" data-insert-type="image" height="321" src="https://cdn.newsbusters.org/styles/blog_image_100_/s3/2026-03/Screenshot%202026-03-04%20143855.png?itok=DsT3Fw3h" title="" width="930" /></p>

<p>DePaul is also partnering on this effort with the liberal media nonprofit Public Narrative, which has been funded by massive left-wing money networks like the MacArthur Foundation, and eBay co-founder Pierre Omidyar. MacArthur — which has doled out millions to causes such as “environmentalist policy, population control,” “racial justice” and “abortion access” <a href="https://www.influencewatch.org/non-profit/john-d-and-catherine-t-macarthur-foundation/">per</a> Influence Watch — has nominally funneled <a href="https://www.macfound.org/grantee/community-media-workshop-3123/">$2,030,300</a> (unadjusted for inflation) between Public Narrative’s founding in 1989 to 2024. Omidyar, who has <a href="https://newsbusters.org/blogs/free-speech/catherine-salgado/2023/06/13/leftist-billionaire-pierre-omidyar-financed-govt">financed efforts</a> to censor <a href="https://newsbusters.org/blogs/business/joseph-vazquez/2025/07/24/breaking-corporation-public-broadcasting-gave-tax-soros">conservative</a> viewpoints on social media and <a href="https://newsbusters.org/blogs/business/renata-kiss/2023/02/10/leftist-billionaire-pierre-omidyar-attempts-reimagining">infuse</a> left-wing dogmatism into U.S. journalism, also gave out a $100,000 grant to Public Narrative in 2024, according to a <a href="https://democracyfund.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/2024-Democracy-Fund-990-PF-FINAL.pdf">990 tax filing</a>.</p>

<p>Public Narrative’s “<a href="https://www.publicnarrative.org/our-mission">Mission</a>” page reads like a DEI factsheet:</p>

<blockquote class="im--blockquote">
<p>We balance the public narrative through <strong>equity, inclusivity</strong> <strong>and authenticity frameworks</strong> in all aspects of media coverage: from storytelling to consumption and the production and promotion of all media forms.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>The "baseline research" for the institute was done in collaboration with a "Black-led" group called <a href="https://www.reparationsnarrativelab.org/">Reparations Media</a>, which as you might expect, seeks to "build narrative power and increase public support for reparations" for African Americans. </p>

<p>Are DePaul’s donors okay with their fortunes being used to fund this kind of radical leftist indoctrination foisted onto students?</p>
